request.subject: RM_CrystalMit

edits.change: The crystal arrangement is fixed on the carapace and identical in every facing: one tall central quartz spire rises on the shell midline at the shoulders just behind the head, flanked by two smaller crystal clusters, one on each side of the spire, at the same relative positions.

In the rear view, seen from behind, the same tall central spire stands on the midline of the carapace with the two smaller clusters on its left and right, so the rear midline carries the spire and not bare stone plates.

In the front view, eyes toward the viewer, the tall central spire rises directly above and behind the head on the midline, with the two smaller clusters at its sides; in side views the spire stands on the top midline of the shell with one smaller cluster visible beside it.

invariants: grey granite-like stone carapace in muted slate, ash and warm-grey tones with mottled speckled surface
eight short jointed stone legs at consistent span
distinct head, small dark eyes, heavy blunt rock-crushing mandibles
glassy, partly translucent quartz crystals, pale and uneven
vanilla RimWorld painterly style, clean dark outline, transparent background
consistent carapace width and length, animal silhouette
request.prompt: A single Crystalmit, a mite-like creature, painted in the vanilla RimWorld animal-texture style: realistic, with a clean dark outline, on a transparent background. Its body is a rounded stone carapace raised on eight short, jointed stone legs, with a distinct head, small dark eyes and one pair of heavy, blunt rock-crushing mandibles. The creature is drawn at one fixed scale: the carapace keeps a consistent width and length, and the eight legs keep a consistent overall span, with broad, rounded haunches at the full body width. The carapace and legs are grey, granite-like stone plates in muted slate, ash and warm-grey tones, with a mottled, weathered, speckled surface. The crystal arrangement is one fixed layout, the same in every facing and turning with the body: a single tall glassy quartz spire rises on the shell midline at the shoulders just behind the head, flanked by two smaller crystal clusters, one on each side of the spire, at the same relative positions. In the front view, eyes toward the viewer, the tall spire rises directly above and behind the head with a small cluster on each side of it. In the rear view, seen from behind, the same tall spire stands on the midline of the carapace with the two smaller clusters to its left and right, so the rear midline carries the spire. In side views the spire stands on the top midline of the shell with one smaller cluster visible beside it. The crystals are pale, partly translucent and uneven, letting light through; between them the hide is mottled stone with small translucent crystalline patches. The crystals rise from the carapace without enlarging or shrinking it, and its silhouette stays clearly that of an animal. Brushwork is visible, shading is soft, tones are muted and natural, highlights on the crystals are small and uneven, and the stone is matte.
